notes: All 9 assertions pass in both configurations for both evals (18/18 vs 18/18): the assertion set is non-discriminating for a capable executor — the old skill already produced structurally equivalent drafts (router SKILL.md, intent-grouped references, unverified banners, verification plan, trap-style evals).

Process differences favor the new skill: both with_skill runs used the bundled scripts (fetch_docs.sh, openapi_summary.py) instead of hand-parsing; fewer fetches (Resend 11 vs 14, Kimi 52 vs 57); far denser endpoint-level uncertainty markers (Resend 132 vs 26 ⚠, Kimi 102 vs 13).

Both old_skill runs independently reported the same gaps — no 'no API key' mode, llms-full.txt not mentioned, OpenAPI only on vendor GitHub, relative link to ../bigmodel-cn, run_eval.py misdescribed — all of which the rewrite already addresses. New-skill feedback is refinement-level: llms-full.txt shortcut, delegation race safeguard, `python -m scripts.package_skill` invocation + pyyaml, what step 4 means in draft-only scope, /docs/llms.txt path variant, multi-product scoping. All applied to the skill after this iteration.

Time/tokens are not apples-to-apples: with_skill runs were +323s and ~+20k tokens, but produced 2-2.3x more reference content (Resend 2,222 vs 1,049 lines; Kimi 3,410 vs 1,505) and each needed two coordinator resumes while waiting on writer sub-agents.

Delegation races (coordinator writing a sub-agent's assigned file, sub-agents overwriting each other) occurred in 3 of 4 runs regardless of version — the strongest signal for a concrete change to write.md (now added: .done markers, never write an assigned path before completion).

Eval feedback for iteration 2: add discriminating assertions (bundled scripts or equivalent used; ⚠ markers at endpoint level ≥ N; verification-status banner at top of SKILL.md; no sub-agent file overwritten), since structure-only assertions saturate.
